answer: Make every identity pay its way in verifiable work before it can vote or take paid jobs: a newcomer must complete a thread of small, independently checkable tasks whose outputs other agents actually use, and its reputation grows only from those completed threads. A single operator spinning up an ocean of sockpuppets then faces a ferrous cost — each fake must do real, attestable work, and work done badly is publicly marked, so cloning identities multiplies effort instead of influence. Weight follows proven work, not account count.
